about: Cross-check cases for the next pound composer (src/calculators/next-pound, part C1), one per leg and for the break-even. Every case is a todo until filled. Never fill a figure from Sumyard's own engine or from memory. Each leg must also be reproducible from its own engine's cross-check (reproducesFrom): the composer adds no arithmetic beyond what docs/money.md, 'Next pound decision (session C0)', lists. Once C1 exists, its crossChecks test shows an unfilled case as a todo and compares a filled one with the composer.
privacy: This repository is public. Enter figures only: amounts, rates, dates, ages and counts. No name, address, employer, scheme, account or policy number, lender reference, or anything else that identifies a person, a pension or a loan. In source, name the kind of document and the provider ("retirement illustration, <provider>, 2026") at most; keep the document itself off the repository.
howToFill: Amounts as pounds strings ("12345.67"), rates as percentage text ("4.5"), dates as YYYY-MM-DD, ages and years as whole numbers. Pension inputs as the optimiser page stores them (pensionMethod 'reliefAtSource', 'netPay' or 'salarySacrifice'; region 'rUK' or 'scotland'); mortgage inputs as docs/mortgage-cross-checks.json describes them, with the effect always 'reduce-term' (CP5). Fill in expected only what the document shows; leave the rest null. Add source and checkedOn (YYYY-MM-DD), both required once any expected value is filled. tolerancePence is the largest difference accepted; change it only with a note in docs/worked-examples.md.

cases.description: X of take-home into the pension at the person's own pay: the extra contribution, the pension it adds and its cost in spendable income (CP3). Source: two payslips or a payroll illustration either side of a one-off contribution, or two take-home figures from an HMRC calculator.

reproducesFrom.note: each of the two take-home figures is an HMRC cross-check case at that contribution

cases.description: As pension-leg-cost with pay inside the personal allowance taper, so the cost per pound of pension is lowest (CP3, edge cases). Same kind of source.

A pot at the horizon split into the tax-free part and the taxed rest at a retirement rate (CP4). Source: a pension provider's retirement illustration, or the worked example on GOV.UK's 'Tax when you get a pension', 'What's tax-free', for the split only (NP-2).

reproducesFrom.note: the pot itself is a compound interest projection; this case checks only the split and the tax

cases.description: A horizon that ends before the access age: the pension column shows no number (CP4). Source: the person's own age and scheme rules.

X overpaid as one lump sum with the payment kept and the term shortened, read at a horizon inside the term: the balance difference and the payments freed (CP5). Source: the same lender illustration as the mortgage case it reproduces.
X above the penalty-free allowance: the overpayment plus its ERC equal X, the rest is cash (CP5). Source: a lender's ERC quote for an overpayment.
X paid into an invested ISA now, grown at one rate with a fee to the horizon, nominal and in today's money (CP6). Source: a provider's projection or a spreadsheet, as compound interest's cases.

reproducesFrom.note: a lump-sum case with a fee

cases.description: The ISA growth rate at which the ISA leg equals the mortgage leg for the same X and horizon (CP7). Source: a spreadsheet goal seek on the mortgage-leg-reduce-term figures.
